purpose: Adds a dismissible post-activation welcome panel to the Dashboard tab guiding first-time users through 3 quick-start actions (Page Caching, JS/CSS Minification, Lazy Loading), plus fixes a cache_settings key mismatch that caused config drift between REST API writes and PHP reads.
riskRationale: Mostly additive UI feature with low-risk bug fix. Main concern is UX overlap with the existing admin welcome notice, which is easy to resolve.

text: Well-structured PR that correctly implements the described plan. The cache_settings key fix is thorough and addresses a genuine inconsistency between REST API writes and PHP reads. The welcome panel follows existing code patterns (FeatureCard, apiCall, user meta). Two important UX issues need resolution before merging: the old admin notice overlaps with the new panel, and step-action failure still dismisses the panel without allowing retry.

reasoning: Two important UX issues should be addressed: (1) the old admin notice overlaps with the new in-panel welcome during the first week post-activation, (2) step-action failure still dismisses the panel, preventing retry. Both fixes are small and isolated.

message: The cache_settings key fix in can_cache_management() correctly aligns the Abilities API read path with the REST API write path, fixing a real config drift bug.
Clean mapping from user meta to show_welcome flag — uses negation directly in wp_localize_script, keeping frontend logic simple.
isEnabled() reads from the global wppoSettings which apiCall('update_settings') mutates on success, keeping the panel reactive without extra state management.
STEPS array is well-factored — declarative, self-contained, and easy to extend with additional onboarding steps.

handleStepAction dismisses the panel even when the update_settings API call fails (catch block). A transient failure (network blip, 500 error) hides the panel permanently for the session, and the user cannot retry the action without refreshing the page.
suggestion: Only dismiss the panel when the step action succeeds. Move setVisible(false) and dismiss_welcome into the try block after the first apiCall succeeds.

message: Both the old admin notice (wppo_show_welcome_notice transient from class-admin-notices.php:109-125) and the new WelcomePanel are activated simultaneously. During the first week after activation, users will see both a dismissible success banner at the top of admin pages AND the welcome panel on the Dashboard tab.
suggestion: Remove the set_transient call for wppo_show_welcome_notice in class-activate.php since the new WelcomePanel supersedes the old notice.

message: The three 'Enable' buttons lack an aria-label to convey which feature they activate. Screen reader users will hear just 'Enable' without context.
suggestion: Add an aria-label attribute using the step label, e.g. aria-label={sprintf(/* translators: %s: feature name */ __('Enable %s', 'performance-optimisation'), step.label)}.

message: Enable buttons have no loading or disabled state. If the API call takes time, there is no visual feedback for the user.
suggestion: Track a loading state per step key (e.g. activatingStep) and disable the button + show a spinner while the API call is in flight.

message: The global wppoSettings.settings mutation on update_settings success is a side effect that creates implicit coupling. WelcomePanel.STEPS.isEnabled reads from the same global, so if a step action succeeds the checkmark renders, but since the panel auto-dismisses this state is never visible.
suggestion: Add a comment documenting the implicit coupling so future maintainers understand that STEPS.isEnabled resolves from the mutating global only matters before dismissal.
